verses.zh: 你们要赞美耶和华！要称谢耶和华，因他本为善；他的慈爱永远长存！
verses.en: Praise the Lord.Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good,and his loyal love endures.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 106. The psalmist recalls Israel’s long history of rebellion against God, despite his mighty saving deeds on their behalf.

verses.zh: 谁能传说耶和华的大能？谁能表明他一切的美德？
verses.en: Who can adequately recount the Lord’s mighty actsor relate all his praiseworthy deeds?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for forever [is] his loyal love.”

verses.zh: 凡遵守公平、常行公义的，这人便为有福！
verses.en: How blessed are those who promote justiceand do what is right all the time.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你用恩惠待你的百姓；求你也用这恩惠记念我，开你的救恩眷顾我，
verses.en: Remember me, O Lord, when you show favor to your people.Pay attention to me, when you deliver,

verses.zh: 使我见你选民的福，乐你国民的乐，与你的产业一同夸耀。
verses.en: so I may see the prosperity[NOTE:1] of your chosen ones,rejoice along with your nation,[NOTE:2] and boast along with the people who belong to you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “[or] cause to be heard all his praise.”
Heb “good.”
Heb “in order that [I may] rejoice with the rejoicing of your nation.”

verses.zh: 我们与我们的祖宗一同犯罪；我们作了孽，行了恶。
verses.en: We have sinned like[NOTE:1] our ancestors;[NOTE:2] we have done wrong, we have done evil.
notes: Heb “with your inheritance.”
Heb “with.”

verses.zh: 我们的祖宗在埃及不明白你的奇事，不记念你丰盛的慈爱，反倒在红海行了悖逆。
verses.en: Our ancestors in Egypt failed to appreciate your miraculous deeds.They failed to remember your many acts of loyal love,and they rebelled at the sea, by the Red Sea.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “fathers” (also in v. 7).

verses.zh: 然而，他因自己的名拯救他们，为要彰显他的大能，
verses.en: Yet he delivered them for the sake of his reputation[NOTE:1] that he might reveal his power.
notes: They rebelled. The psalmist recalls the people’s complaint recorded in Exod 14:12.tn Heb “Reed Sea” (also in vv. 9, 22). “Reed Sea” (or “Sea of Reeds”) is a more accurate rendering of the Hebrew expression יָם סוּף (yam suf), traditionally translated “Red Sea.” See the note on the term “Red Sea” in Exod 13:18.

verses.zh: 并且斥责红海，海便干了；他带领他们经过深处，如同经过旷野。
verses.en: He shouted at[NOTE:1] the Red Sea and it dried up;he led them through the deep water as if it were a desert.
notes: Heb “his name,” which here stands metonymically for God’s reputation.

verses.zh: 他拯救他们脱离恨他们人的手，从仇敌手中救赎他们。
verses.en: He delivered them from the power[NOTE:1] of the one who hated themand rescued[NOTE:2] them from the power[NOTE:3] of the enemy.
notes: Or “rebuked.”
Heb “hand.”
Or “redeemed.”

verses.zh: 水淹没他们的敌人，没有一个存留。
verses.en: The water covered their enemies;not even one of them survived.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 那时，他们才信了他的话，歌唱赞美他。
verses.en: They believed his promises;[NOTE:1] they sang praises to him.
notes: Heb “remained.”

verses.zh: 等不多时，他们就忘了他的作为，不仰望他的指教，
verses.en: They quickly forgot what he had done;[NOTE:1] they did not wait for his instructions.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “his words.”
Heb “his works.”

verses.zh: 反倒在旷野大起欲心，在荒地试探　神。
verses.en: In the wilderness they had an insatiable craving[NOTE:1] for meat;[NOTE:2] they challenged God[NOTE:3] in the wastelands.
notes: Heb “his counsel.”
They had an insatiable craving. This is described in Num 11:4-35.
Heb “they craved [with] a craving.”

verses.zh: 他将他们所求的赐给他们，却使他们的心灵软弱。
verses.en: He granted their request,then struck them with a disease.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they tested God.”

verses.zh: 他们又在营中嫉妒摩西和耶和华的圣者亚伦。
verses.en: In the camp they resented[NOTE:1] Mosesand Aaron the Lord’s holy priest.[NOTE:2]
notes: Disease. See Num 11:33-34, where this plague is described.tn Heb “and he sent leanness into their being.”
Or “envied.”

verses.zh: 地裂开，吞下大坍，掩盖亚比兰一党的人。
verses.en: The earth opened up and swallowed Dathan;[NOTE:1]it engulfed[NOTE:2] the group led by Abiram.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the holy one of the Lord.”
Or “covered.”
Or “the assembly of Abiram.”

verses.zh: 有火在他们的党中发起；有火焰烧毁了恶人。
verses.en: Fire burned their group;the flames scorched the wicked.[NOTE:1]
notes: Verses 16-18 describe the events of Num 16:1-40.

verses.zh: 他们在何烈山造了牛犊，叩拜铸成的像。
verses.en: They made an image of a calf at Horeb[NOTE:1]and worshiped a metal idol.
notes: Heb “their glory.” According to an ancient Hebrew scribal tradition, the text originally read “his glory” or “my glory.” In Jer 2:11 the Lord states that his people (Israel) exchanged “their glory” (a reference to the Lord) for worthless idols.

verses.zh: 如此将他们荣耀的主换为吃草之牛的像，
verses.en: They traded their majestic God[NOTE:1] for the image of an ox that eats grass.
notes: Heb “forgot.”

verses.zh: 忘了　神―他们的救主；他曾在埃及行大事，
verses.en: They rejected[NOTE:1] the God who delivered them,the one who performed great deeds in Egypt,
notes: Or “awe-inspiring acts.”

verses.zh: 在含地行奇事，在红海行可畏的事。
verses.en: amazing feats in the land of Ham,mighty acts[NOTE:1] by the Red Sea.
notes: Heb “and he said.”

verses.zh: 所以，他说要灭绝他们；若非有他所拣选的摩西站在当中（原文是破口），使他的忿怒转消，恐怕他就灭绝他们。
verses.en: He threatened[NOTE:1] to destroy them,but[NOTE:2] Moses, his chosen one, interceded with him[NOTE:3] and turned back his destructive anger.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “if not,” that is, “[and would have] if [Moses] had not.”
Heb “stood in the gap before him.”
Heb “to turn back his anger from destroying.”sn Verses 19-23 describe the events of Exod 32:1-35.
Heb “a land of delight” (see also Jer 3:19; Zech 7:14).

verses.zh: 他们又藐视那美地，不信他的话，
verses.en: They rejected the fruitful land;[NOTE:1] they did not believe his promise.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “his word.”
They grumbled in their tents. See Deut 1:27.

verses.zh: 在自己帐棚内发怨言，不听耶和华的声音。
verses.en: They grumbled in their tents;[NOTE:1] they did not obey[NOTE:2] the Lord.
notes: Heb “did not listen to the voice of.”

Heb “and he lifted his hand to [or “concerning”] them.” The idiom “to lift a hand” here refers to swearing an oath. One would sometimes solemnly lift one’s hand when making such a vow (see Ezek 20:5-6, 15).

verses.zh: 所以，他对他们起誓：必叫他们倒在旷野，
verses.en: So he made a solemn vow[NOTE:1] that he would make them die[NOTE:2] in the wilderness,
notes: Heb “to cause them to fall.”
Or “offspring”; Heb “seed.”

verses.zh: 叫他们的后裔倒在列国之中，分散在各地。
verses.en: make their descendants[NOTE:1] die[NOTE:2] among the nations,and scatter them among foreign lands.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and to cause their offspring to fall.” Some emend the verb to “scatter” to form tighter parallelism with the following line (cf. NRSV “disperse”).
Heb “among the lands.” The word “foreign” is supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “joined themselves to.”sn They worshiped Baal of Peor. See Num 25:3, 5. Baal of Peor was a local manifestation of the Canaanite deity Baal located at Peor.

verses.zh: 他们又与巴力•毗珥连合，且吃了祭死神（或译：人）的物。
verses.en: They worshiped[NOTE:1] Baal of Peorand ate sacrifices offered to the dead.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here “the dead” may refer to deceased ancestors (see Deut 26:14). Another option is to understand the term as a derogatory reference to the various deities which the Israelites worshiped at Peor along with Baal (see Num 25:2 and L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 49).

Heb “They made angry [him].” The pronominal suffix is omitted here, but does appear in a few medieval Hebrew mss. Perhaps it was accidentally left off, an original וַיַּכְעִיסוּהוּ (vayyakhʿisuhu) being misread as וַיַּכְעִיסוּ (vayyakhʿisu). In the translation the referent of the pronominal suffix (the Lord) has been specified for clarity to avoid confusion with Baal of Peor (mentioned in the previous verse).

verses.zh: 他们这样行，惹耶和华发怒，便有瘟疫流行在他们中间。
verses.en: They made the Lord angry[NOTE:1] by their actions,and a plague broke out among them.
notes: The intervention of Phinehas is recounted in Num 25:7-8.

verses.zh: 那时，非尼哈站起，刑罚恶人，瘟疫这才止息。
verses.en: Phinehas took a stand and intervened,[NOTE:1] and the plague subsided.
notes: Heb “and it was reckoned to him for righteousness, to a generation and a generation forever.” The verb חָשַׁב (khashav, “to reckon”) is collocated with צְדָקָה (tsedaqah, “righteousness”) only in Ps 106:31 and Gen 15:6, where God credits Abram’s faith as righteousness.

verses.zh: 那就算为他的义，世世代代，直到永远。
verses.en: This was credited to Phinehas as a righteous actfor all generations to come.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “there was harm to Moses.”

verses.zh: 他们在米利巴水又叫耶和华发怒，甚至摩西也受了亏损，
verses.en: They made him angry by the waters of Meribah,and Moses suffered[NOTE:1] because of them,
notes: The Hebrew text vocalizes the form as הִמְרוּ (himru), a Hiphil from מָרָה (marah, “to behave rebelliously”), but the verb fits better with the object (“his spirit”) if it is revocalized as הֵמֵרוּ (hemeru), a Hiphil from מָרַר (marar, “to be bitter”). The Israelites “embittered” Moses’ “spirit” in the sense that they aroused his temper with their complaints.

verses.zh: 是因他们惹动他的灵，摩西（原文是他）用嘴说了急躁的话。
verses.en: for they aroused[NOTE:1] his temper,[NOTE:2] and he spoke rashly.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his spirit.”
The Hebrew text adds “with his lips,” but this has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.sn Verses 32-33 allude to the events of Num 20:1-13.
That is, the nations of Canaan.

verses.zh: 他们不照耶和华所吩咐的灭绝外邦人，
verses.en: They did not destroy the nations,[NOTE:1] as the Lord had commanded them to do.
notes: Heb “their deeds.”

verses.zh: 反与他们混杂相合，学习他们的行为，
verses.en: They mixed in with the nationsand learned their ways.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “served.”

verses.zh: 事奉他们的偶像，这就成了自己的网罗，
verses.en: They worshiped[NOTE:1] their idols,which became a snare to them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Became a snare. See Exod 23:33; Judg 2:3.
The Hebrew term שֵׁדִים (shedim, “demons”) occurs only here and in Deut 32:17. Some type of lesser deity is probably in view.

verses.zh: 把自己的儿女祭祀鬼魔，
verses.en: They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons.[NOTE:1]
notes: Num 35:33-34 explains that bloodshed defiles a land.

verses.zh: 流无辜人的血，就是自己儿女的血，把他们祭祀迦南的偶像，那地就被血污秽了。
verses.en: They shed innocent blood—the blood of their sons and daughters,whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan.The land was polluted by bloodshed.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they committed adultery in their actions.” This means that they were unfaithful to the Lord (see Ps 73:27).

verses.zh: 这样，他们被自己所做的污秽了，在行为上犯了邪淫。
verses.en: They were defiled by their deedsand unfaithful in their actions.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the anger of the Lord burned against his people.”

verses.zh: 所以，耶和华的怒气向他的百姓发作，憎恶他的产业，
verses.en: So the Lord was angry with his people[NOTE:1] and despised the people who belonged to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “his inheritance.”
Heb “gave them into the hand of.”

verses.zh: 将他们交在外邦人的手里；恨他们的人就辖制他们。
verses.en: He handed them over to[NOTE:1] the nations,and those who hated them ruled over them.
notes: Heb “they were subdued under their hand.”

verses.zh: 他们的仇敌也欺压他们，他们就伏在敌人手下。
verses.en: Their enemies oppressed them;they were subject to their authority.[NOTE:1]
notes: The prefixed verbal form is either preterite or imperfect, in which case it is customary, describing repeated action in past time (“he would deliver”).

verses.zh: 他屡次搭救他们，他们却设谋背逆，因自己的罪孽降为卑下。
verses.en: Many times he delivered[NOTE:1] them,but they had a rebellious attitude[NOTE:2] and degraded themselves[NOTE:3] by their sin.
notes: Heb “but they rebelled in their counsel.” The prefixed verbal form is either preterite or imperfect, in which case it is customary, describing repeated action in past time (“they would have a rebellious attitude”).
Heb “they sank down.” The Hebrew verb מָכַךְ (makhakh, “to lower; to sink”) occurs only here in the Qal.
The Niphal of נָחַם (nakham) refers here to God relenting from a punishment already underway.

verses.zh: 然而，他听见他们哀告的时候，就眷顾他们的急难，
verses.en: Yet he took notice of their distress,when he heard their cry for help.

verses.zh: 为他们记念他的约，照他丰盛的慈爱后悔。
verses.en: He remembered his covenant with themand relented[NOTE:1] because of his great loyal love.
notes: Or “captors.”

verses.zh: 他也使他们在凡掳掠他们的人面前蒙怜恤。
verses.en: He caused all their conquerors[NOTE:1] to have pity on them.
notes: Heb “to give thanks.” The infinitive construct indicates result after the imperative.

verses.zh: 耶和华―我们的　神啊，求你拯救我们，从外邦中招聚我们，我们好称赞你的圣名，以赞美你为夸胜。
verses.en: Deliver us, O Lord, our God.Gather us from among the nations.Then we will give thanks[NOTE:1] to your holy name,and boast about your praiseworthy deeds.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to boast in your praise.”
Heb “[be] blessed.” See Pss 18:46; 28:6; 31:21.

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的　神是应当称颂的，从亘古直到永远。愿众民都说：阿们！你们要赞美耶和华！
verses.en: The Lord God of Israel deserves praise,[NOTE:1] in the future and forevermore.[NOTE:2] Let all the people say, “We agree![NOTE:3] Praise the Lord!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “from everlasting to everlasting.”
Heb “surely” (אָמֵן,ʾamen), traditionally transliterated “amen.”

The final verse (v. 48) is a conclusion to this fourth “book” (or major editorial division) of the Psalter. Similar statements appear at or near the end of each of the first, second and third “books” of the Psalter (see Pss 41:13; 72:18-19; 89:52, respectively).

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- If Psalm 105 is a history of YHWH's salvation/deliverance of Abraham and his descendants; then
Psalm 106 is a history of their continuous rebellion. YHWH is faithful; His people are faithless (cf. Nehemiah 9)!

- The books of Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, and Judges are the focus of the vast
majority of the historical allusions. Here is a list of them.

- Ps. 106:9 ‒ Exod. 14:21

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 106:1-3

1Praise the Lord!

Oh give thanks to the Lord, for He is good;

For His lovingkindness is
everlasting.

2Who can speak of
the mighty deeds of the Lord,

Or can show forth all His
praise?

3How blessed are
those who keep justice,

Who practice righteousness at
all times!

106:1-3 This first strophe has two themes.

- description of YHWH

- He is good (BDB 373 II, cf. 2 Chr. 5:13; 7:3; Ps. 25:8; 86:5; 100:5; 107:1; 118:1,29; 145:9)

- His lovingkindness is everlasting (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS [hesed]) and
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ['olam])

- description of His true followers

- they speak of His mighty deeds

- they praise Him

- they keep justice (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUSTICE, and JUDGMENT)

- they (see LXX, Peshitta, Vulgate, MT, "he") practice righteousness (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS)

This description is crucial because what follows is repeated historical allusion to Israel's faithlessness.

106:1 The Psalm begins and ends with commands to praise.

- praise ‒ BDB 237, KB 248, Piel IMPERATIVE, Ps. 106:1, cf. 107:1; 118:1,29; 136:1

- give thanks (lit. praise) ‒ BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, Ps. 106:1, cf. 1 Chr. 16:41

- praise ‒ same as #1, Ps. 106:48

Faithful followers praise Him by how they speak of Him and how they live like Him! Blessed is
the person who obeys the Lord (cf. Psalm 1).

106:2 "mighty deeds" This refers to YHWH's acts of deliverance and provision. This theme is
continued from Psalm 105 (see full note on the seven occurrences in Psalm 105 at 105:1-7 notes).

- mighty deeds, Ps. 106:2 ‒ BDB 150, cf. Deut. 3:24; Ps. 20:6; 71:16; 145:4,12; 150:2; Isa. 63:15

- wonders, Ps. 106:7 ‒ BDB 810 (see note at Ps. 105:1-7)

- works, Ps. 106:13 ‒ BDB 795, cf. Josh. 24:31; Ps. 33:4; 93:5

- great things, Ps. 106:21 ‒ BDB 152, i.e., esp. in Egypt, cf. Deut. 10:21; here; but also of YHWH's
other acts in Job 5:9; 9:10; 37:5; Ps. 71:19; 126:2

- wonders, Ps. 106:22 ‒ same as #2

- wonders (lit. "terrible things" ), Ps. 106:22 ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Niphal PARTICIPLE,
cf. Deut. 10:21; 2 Sam. 7:23; 1 Chr. 17:21; Ps. 66:3; 145:6; Isa. 64:3

106:3 "at all times" This is a crucial aspect to discipleship. Godly living is a full-time task! Now, remember
this is an OT setting. It reflects "the two ways" of Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1. The quote at Gal. 3:10-12 illustrates
the performance-based OT covenant. Even though NT believers are not under the OT (cf. Acts 15), once we know

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

18:10 "who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire" This is a reference to the worship
of the fertility god, Molech. In Israel the firstborn (cf. Exodus 13) was to be given to YHWH to serve Him.
In Canaan the firstborn was to be sacrificed by fire to Molech in order to insure fertility, (cf. Deut. 12:31;
Lev. 18:21). There is even one account in 2 Kgs. 21:6 where God's people worshiped this false fertility god! It also
possibly relates somehow to knowing the future (cf. 2 Kgs. 3:26:27). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH.

▣ "divination" This is from the Hebrew root for "divine" (BDB 890, cf. Num. 22:7; 23:23; Ezek. 21:21;
2 Kgs. 17:17). It is the general term describing several different methods, but all intent on determining the will of a
deity by mechanical or natural means, such as examining the livers of sheep or casting arrows. It is based on the
pagan worldview that there is information about the future hidden in natural events and that gifted humans
(i.e., false prophets, e.g., Jer. 27:9; 29:8; Ezek. 13:9; 22:28) know it and influence this future.

▣ "one who practices witchcraft" This term (BDB 778 II, KB 857) is related to the term "cloud" (BDB 777).
Linguists think the term is related to sound:

- the hum of insects

- sound of wind in the trees

- unknown etymology (if cloud, then related to sight)

The parallel passage in Moses' writings which prohibits these same pagan practices is in
Lev. 19:26-20:8 (see esp. 19:26). This same term is also found in Jdgs. 9:37; 2 Kgs. 21:6; 2 Chr. 33:6; Isa. 2:6; 57:3; Jer. 27:9; Micah 5:12.

▣ "one who interprets omens" The meaning of this term (BDB 638 II, KB 690) is uncertain. In Syrian
it means "to murmur an obscure incantation" (KB 690). The root has several usages:

- serpent ‒ BDB 638 I

- VERB in Piel only, (BDB 638 II) meaning :

- practice divination

- observe signs/omens

- copper ‒ bronze, BDB 638 III

- unknown ‒ BDB 638 IV

▣ "a sorcerer" This term (BDB 506, KB 503) basically means "to cut up"

- as in the shredding of ingredients for a magical potion

- cutting oneself as a way of getting the deity's attention (i.e., Syrian usage, cf. 1 Kgs. 18:28)

- This term was used to describe

- Pharaoh's wise men in Exod. 7:11

- Nebuchadnezzar's wise men in Dan. 2:2

18:11 "one who casts a spell" This literally is "to tie knots," "to be allied with," or "join together" (BDB 287,
KB 287). In Psalm 58:5 and Eccl. 10:11 it refers to snake charming. A slightly different vocalization describes a
Babylonian false wise man in Isa. 47:8-11.

▣ "mediums" The PARTICIPLE'S (BDB 981, KB 1371) basic meaning is to "ask"
or "inquire." Here, to inquire of the spirit realm (e.g., YHWH, Josh. 9:14 or idols, Hosea 4:12).

The first NOUN, "medium" (BDB 15) is a difficult term to define. Some see
the term as it is used in Lev. 19:31; 20:6,27 as (1) a pit or grave where spirits are lured, (2) form of "father" which
refers to ancestor worship. It is translated in the LXX in Isa. 8:19 as "ventriloquist." Because of this and Isa. 29:4
some think it means "to chirp" or "to mutter." This would imply to "talk with a different voice." However, from
1 Sam. 28:7-9, it is related to the ability to call or talk to someone in the ground or to communicate with the dead
or spirits of the underworld, i.e., necromancy.

The second NOUN, "spiritists" (BDB 396) was a form of the Hebrew word
"to know" (BDB 395). It refers to one who has knowledge of the spiritual realm or has contact with those in the
spiritual realm who have knowledge (cf. Isa. 8:19; 19:3).

▣ "one who calls up the dead" This phrase is a combination of two Qal PARTICIPLES
(BDB 205, KB 233, "to ask" and BDB 559, KB 562, "the dead ones"). In context it refers to mediums and "spiritists." These
elite, supposedly gifted, people contact the dead for information about the future and the power to affect it.

All ancient cultures believed in an afterlife. For many in the ANE this had two possibilities:

- ancestor worship where the spirits of family members could affect the present and future

- the power of physical (stars, forces of nature) or spiritual (demons, demigods) could be utilized to know and affect personal destinies

Ps. 106:28 This refers to Israel's idolatry with Ba'al at Baal-peor (cf. Num. 25:1-3; 31:16).

106:36 "Which became a snare" This word, "snare" (BDB 430), is a reference to an animal trap
(lit. "bait" or "lure"). It was used as imagery for the temptation to Canaanite fertility worship
(cf. Exod. 23:33; Deut. 7:16; Jdgs. 2:3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

106:37-38 This refers to the worship of the fertility god, Molech.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

106:37 "demons" This (BDB 993) refers to pagan gods (cf. Deut. 32:17). The word is used only twice in
the OT. It is possibly a loan word from Aramaic. The concept of pagan idols as demons is seen in the NT in
1 Cor. 10:19-20 and Rev. 9:20.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS and DEMONS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEMONIC IN THE OT

106:38 "the land was polluted" The land of Canaan was polluted by the Canaanites (cf. Gen. 15:16) and
now by the Israelites (cf. Num. 35:33-34; Jer. 3:2-10). Canaan belonged to YHWH. It was His land.

▣ "with blood" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

106:39 "played the harlot" This (BDB 275, KB 275, Qal IMPERFECT with waw) is a
Hebrew idiom for idolatrous worship (cf. Jdgs. 2:17; Ezekiel 23; Hosea 5:3). It is based on the imagery of YHWH as Father
and Israel as wife (cf. Hosea 1-3). To go after another god was viewed as "spiritual adultery" (cf. Exod. 34:15; Num. 15:39;
Ps. 73:27; Hosea 4:12; 9:1). Sometimes the imagery is both figurative and literal because many/most of the fertility worship
was by imitation magic (i.e., sexual activity in the name of and at the site of worship).
